props.gloss_en: even if the king greets him [while he prays], he should not respond
Rav Yosef: they taught this only of kings of Israel
Rav Yosef: but for kings of the nations of the world, he interrupts [his prayer]
the baraita: one praying who sees a violent man or a carriage coming toward him does not interrupt, but shortens [his prayer] and moves aside
the baraita speaks where it is possible to shorten -- then he shortens; if not, he interrupts
a pious man was praying on the road; an officer came and greeted him, and he did not return the greeting

the officer: good-for-nothing, is it not written in your Torah 'only take heed and guard your soul' (Deut 4:9) and 'guard yourselves well' (Deut 4:15)? why did you not return my greeting? had I cut off your head, who would have demanded your blood from me?
at once the officer was appeased, and the pious man went home in peace

schemas.gloss_en: the officer concedes he would not return a friend's greeting before a king of flesh and blood, for they would cut off his head; ומה אתה שהיית עומד לפני מלך בשר ודם שהיום כאן ומחר בקבר כך, אני שהייתי עומד לפני מלך מלכי המלכים הקדוש ברוך הוא שהוא חי וקיים לעד -- על אחת כמה וכמה

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: המתפלל וראה אנס בא כנגדו... לא יהא מפסיק אלא מקצר ועולה -- facing even a violent man he does not interrupt, against Rav Yosef's 'he interrupts'

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דאפשר לקצר (יקצר, ואם לאו -- פוסק) -- the baraita speaks where he can shorten; where he cannot, he interrupts, as Rav Yosef said (= p_efshar_lekatzer)

objections.gloss_en: רק השמר לך ושמור נפשך... למה לא החזרת לי שלום? -- your Torah commands you to guard your life, yet you ignored my greeting and risked it

answered_by.gloss_en: והלא דברים קל וחומר (= kv_melech_malchei_hamelachim) -- and at once the officer was appeased (33a.2)
